instagram_diagnostic_note: As of 2026-08-23: INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH for IMAGE containers still returns 403 code 4 (Application request limit reached) on every attempt (solo, freshly-created, FINISHED-status container included) across 6+ attempts spanning 19+ hours. HOWEVER, video/Reel publishing (daily_queue.json flow, media_type=REELS) succeeded cleanly on first attempt today. This looks like a persistent block specific to the IMAGE publish endpoint for this app/account, not a general or time-based rate limit. Do not keep blind-retrying image publishes every run; retry at most once per day and flag to user if it persists beyond ~1 week — may need Meta app review or re-authorization specific to photo publishing. As of 2026-08-24: still blocked on daily single-retry attempt for a newly-created image container (gyms post). Now confirmed blocked 3 consecutive days (08-22, 08-23, 08-24) despite video/Reel publishing continuing to work fine on the same account. This has crossed from "wait it out" into "likely needs action" — flagging to user per standing instructions. As of 2026-08-25: still blocked, now 4 consecutive days (08-22 through 08-25). Fresh container test on a brand-new image (2026-08-25-01-general) failed identically with 403 code 4. The 30-item promo batch (ig-creation-ids.json) was not re-tested today since its creation_ids are now 3+ days stale and the same account/endpoint just failed on a fresh container seconds earlier — re-testing would only reconfirm the same block. This is well past the 1-week soft threshold from the original diagnostic; user should check whether the Instagram/Facebook connection in Composio needs re-authorization or the app needs Meta review for instagram_content_publish. As of 2026-08-26: still blocked, now 5 consecutive days (08-22 through 08-26). Fresh container test (same 2026-08-25-01-general image, new creation_id 18090747329237571) failed identically with 403 code 4. No new Drive files today (28/28 already in manifest). Already flagged to user; not re-flagging daily unless it clears or reaches ~2 weeks.
